newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian firms in talks to buy Iraqi oil - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian firms in talks to buy Iraqi oil - traders.

text.p: A group of Russian companies is in talks with Baghdad about buying Iraqi oil under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations and could sign contracts next week, Russian industry sources said on Wednesday.
Yuri Agababov, deputy director of oil and equipment supplier Zarubezhneft, said Russia could sign contracts for around 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) but said it was too early to pin down figures.

"I think around 100,000 barrels per day is a realistic amount, but you really should not be talking about concrete figures yet because it all depends on the pace and outcome of negotiations," he said.
"We will buy Iraqi oil, yes. And we will participate on equal terms with all the other companies (in the bidding)."
He said Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry had asked Zarubezhneft to act as coordinator and that the Russian side would hold talks on contracts next week.
Agababov named the other Russian companies interested in buying Iraqi oil as Mashinoimport, Nafta-Moskva, Rosneft, Rosnefteimpex and MES (International Economic Coooperation).
Alfa-Eko and Tatneft might also participate, he said.
A senior official at Mashinoimport who declined to be identified but said he was part of negotiations said the Russian side was interested in buying "as much as there is".
"We expect a contract to be signed possibly in several days," he added.
When asked what multiple of 100,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude Russia could buy, he said, "Multiply by five. Why not?"
But Agababov said that that number was unrealistic.
Both men said Russia would not create a consortium to buy Iraqi crude and that contracts would be individually negotiated.
